Content: Work will be done for the good of the community. We have faced what is inevitable, and have enhanced our community connections so everyone has what they need.
Hands are used to getting dirty. To cook. To garden. To paint. To build. This becomes core and central to one's time spent.
Work is done for purpose and contribution.
Work and life intersect. There is the possibility of not having a job for the sake of survival.
Work is now understood and defined in a much more expansive way that includes caring, creating beauty and art, and all the things it takes to have a healthy community
Workweeks can be 25 hours and domestic and agricultural work is valued at the same level of respect and compensation as what we called professional' work in 2024.
There's no 9-5, there are no jobs, work.
Folks who were disconnected have reconnected and are part of the community.
We are not overworking or burnt out. It's not a thing.

An important thing happened along the last few decades. We finally figured out that workplaces are communities even as they hold important boundaries as workplaces. We found ways to organize work around strengths and talents and contributions... and to meet people's deep desire for belonging without asking that organizations or workplaces be more than that. Part of that solving was realizing that we needed to put less pressure on workplaces to fill needs for community belonging.

We have stopped always using law, standard policy, and other guidance as a way to say no, and we have moved to a system that is embedded in yes's when it meets the vision, mission, values, and purpose of an organization and the peoples and communities served.
We see and care for the value of people and what they bring to the table. We value togetherness, kindness, compassion, and ensure that is written into our programmatic scopes.

We invite traditions, customs, and widsoms of people. They have a place in everyday organizational life. Tribal Elders have places to be and are welcomed and their counsel is asked for and considered. Elders of all backgrounds have roles in organizaitons - elders-in-residence.
Culture is no longer a department, but a set of standards and practices built into each position and program - and more importantly practiced.
Trauma and healing programs have been written into strategic planning and then implemented.
There is healing being generated in tribal communities and then these leaders move to offer and support healing in communities beyond tribal reservation boundaries.

These professionals are the most trauma-informed team members in the whole organization and the needs of employees and their families are considered and well balanced with the needs of the organization. An organization/institution only focus has come to feel foreign/strange/out of place. Human resources workers know the people that come to work - their names and gifts and assets. They consistently practice cultivating the conditions that keep efforts moving with flow – easily navigating ways we are all leaders and worker bees.
Collaboration! Working as a collective.
Co-existence, understanding, political, economic acceptance without judgment.
Value across all types of knowledge and labor, trade, technical, academic
We believe all work is good work and all jobs are good jobs–and value and treat people accordingly.
People live into their purpose every day. You work to live into a purpose. Not to live.

Work would be oriented to a collected and common good no matter what you did. We would take the needed time for that. We will be able to focus – because we know other people are tending their projects. Community would operate and connect a lot like petals of a flower. We would take the time to make food delicious. We would teach, learn, and learn to teach. Everyone is valued for whatever it is they bring.

Less-desirable jobs are worked within friend groups on a yearly/monthly rotational basis. Music and laughter is encouraged through this work. Friend group holidays are taken after the work shift is completed.

There is role fluidity, and people’s spirits are free to play. We trust wisdom holders. We are curious, we explore, we welcome, and we answer calls of need. This is how space for collective wholeness is created. We all have what we need to be well.
Purpose, intention, and trade align because we longer determine which careers are worth more.
Jobs are rotating and many mingas are actively building houses, schools, hospitals and roads.
Everyone has access to meaningful work in their communities, our ability to sustain and care for ourselves is independent of the work we choose to undertake.
Every day is casual Friday.
Everyone has a good job, but also having one’s underlying purpose can help fulfill you no matter what you do. Jobs are no longer labeled as “menial” because all labor is valued equally.
Everyone is paid a livable wage.

The day starts with a community gathering where we share gratitude for our land and each other. We then share preparing a meal together. There are elders and children safely resting and playing among the morning chatter and cooking. We sit together and enjoy company before setting our intentions for the day. Some of us work, some tend, all cooperate because we know our livelihood depends on it. Should there be deviation from the commonly agreed upon community norms, our matriarchs lead the newly designed “generative reparations process.” The process will build community and heal wrongs. We work, trade and build community with other communities that are similar, but different. We understand that we embody the web of life.
Labor is about tending to cultural lifeways i.e. caring for waters, caring for elders.
Jobs based on talents and gifts.

Science is still important. How do we provide without money? Trading in cyclical community. People who grow food teach children how to and science of growing. Health care traded for food…Creating economy in that way. We’re not trading money, we trade services. Gardens, water, children, reusing existing infrastructure and resources.

Keep AI in some way. We don't have to toil all the time. Nature doesn’t need us, just needs us to respect it and be part of it. People are Producing beautiful things for the sake of it- Trade and share with each other in the beauty…
There are no obstacles to sharing well-being. Let the work be based on the things that each person loves.
Original of Translation: No hay obstáculos para compartir el bienestar. Que los trabajos sean a partir de las cosas que cada cual ame.

Content: Good materials are for everyone
We all help each other instead of organizations
Original of Translation: Todos nos ayudamos en vez de organizaciones.

Content: Work is collective and we produce what we share
Original of Translation: Trabajar es colectivo y producimos lo que compartimos.

Content: Kindness, love, respect, humility is how we conduct ourselves. Love initiated everything – engineers, construction workers, scientists.
A foundation of security in relationships and resources in a way that's more so based out of trust. So that people can do and be what they need.
Workers have ownership of the fruits of their labor
People are invited to move towards what draws them and trust that everything that is needed will be covered.

There is organized preparedness to be able to respond to whatever might happen. There are connections of mutual aid that the community can rely on. People trade what is needed without having to rely on money.

We accelerate 150 years in 4 years. AI is eliminating work, so there are no salaried jobs. We are free to be in community service, and service of each other. There is a producer, maker economy. We make the tools, grow the food and all of the things we would normally buy in a cash economy.

We believe we can work together. We are able to remain calm and stay connected to a belief that we have everything that we need.  We tell stories about how we remembered to stay calm, figure out who’s who – and move forward for everyone.

Horizon - collective resistance. How do we shape that? How do we go back to what we were before? Before we were separated. Memory of being children, of play. Now we have opportunity to build what we want for that horizon.
Resourcefulness of immigrant communities with medicine within us.

How do we see it?
Many different colors together–many diverse pieces integrated
This movement, migration, and integration creating community and love. 
Offering balm to the yearning within us.

That work is something that moves to a word like care or tending—that work becomes a natural kuleana—that people know how to tend and take care because it’s been passed down through art, mele, ʻoli, and story.

Work is something we all do together—we work as a family, a group, a cohort—that there is a place for everyone in this tending—young people work next to their elders because that is how we learn—from each other, through practice, through story, through knowing what we do now plants the seeds for all who come after
Simplifications for hiring, opportunity, and how we exist

Hyperabundance. People let go of striving for domination over resources, and instead are comfortable sharing with one another.  We feel a sense of ownership and responsibility to take care of everything/one and be compassionate. We will be more independent than we’ve ever been but more connected than we have been. Food is grown locally, people take turns sharing in the roles that maintain their communities (and this is seen as honorable), but also have space to pursue their own interests. Technology is used sparingly. The age of excess is over.

We have learned how to weave and learn from each others’ ways.  Stories are shared and told freely.  They are education.  They are highly valued.  People are constantly in relationship with the kind of ancestor they want to be.

Scale is now very different.  Governance, exchange, and care is happening at a different scale.  We’ve learned that attending to collective needs has to be local.  People will value knowing the ecology of what we exist in.  We create constant conditions for regrowth.  Scale is related to our “line of sight”  in relationship to what we “know intuitively” is beyond it. In other words, governance happens within our line of sight – but with responsibility to what we know is beyond it.

People still have memories of the boats we worked on, the places we lived, the things we did and created.  Our ancestors will KNOW us.  We will navigate the multiverse with purpose – and understand that we don’t control any of it, but we can live into it.
People use hammers.  They build things with their hands.  No one thinks 3D printers are all that great in the future.  We value what we build with our hands.
There are bulletins everywhere that say things - someone’s birthday, what’s happening in the neighborhood, important notices, and information that is always up-to-date, always accurate.
People strive to be like Harriet Tubman, not “influencers”

I have a sense that we are already smart enough, advanced enough. There isn’t anything that we need to make these things happen…we could do it, gathering the will, creating critical mass and movement. It’s not beyond us

The use and practice of our hands. We have gone back to handwritten letters, and reading the physical newspaper. Notes are written again in a spiral notebook. We have released some aspects of our interdependence with technology in small ways.

We followed the seasons. We had to slow down in the winter, naturally, because there was less to go around, and everyone took care of the shared resources - and if so, there was enough to meet everyone’s needs, no hoarding was necessary.
Things are in place that our only responsibility is to love our children, and the backs of our cradle board are made from Cedar, a tree with a deep and interconnected root system.
Everyone contributes. Their roles are essential and not connected to their ability to have their needs met or thrive. There is ease, connectedness, safety, and being on purpose.

Our priority and collective work becomes the well-being of the community and nature. We live with respect for nature and resources. We consume and use what we need with an understanding of limitations.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: Coexistence through local food space, shared housing, people of multiple generations sharing knowledge, know how, practical things that are produced.

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: There will be open spaces, nature, fresh air.  People don’t worry about making rent, time running out, health care.  We have slowed down and taken care of what is needed in our communities.  Communities are diverse.  There is music…no one is burdened by displacement.  You choose where you fit.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We rest collectively.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: Everyone lives with purpose.
People will operate in smaller connected circles.  It will help us be more efficient and in good relationship with resource.
Skill develops in relationship to need.  People are curious and want to learn how to fill the voids that are needed.
We remember that triangles are the strongest structures.  Curiosity, Acceptance, and Community are what life is built on.  We see that as the triangle that guides and supports us.
Through laughter and playfulness, we generate out of box thinking.
We use collective intention circles for problem solving. To solve major health issues.People can teleport themselves. We collectively share resources of all kinds.

People share their gifts and we are so connected with one another through a felt sense of what each other needs and what we can do to help meet those needs. There is an unspoken sharing of energy. Living from an honorable harvest. Listening to the water and minerals who could choose not to share themselves with us if it was not the right thing to do.
We are enough. There is enough.
We are trading for what we need.
Deep listening is practiced all the time.  Witnessing, intuiting, playing music, conversation.
We have room for friction, dissonance, being transgressive, being wild, breaking the rules. This creates safety also. We value those who step outside of the norms.
I see us moving in 4th dimensional ways of engaging, coming from a place of reconnecting with ancient ways of doing things, following collapse.
Operate from a place of individual and collective belonging.
Sustainable common good

The future is a wound we all have the privilege of healing. It’s not an easy process but with intentionality and hope, it can be brought together. As gruesome as a wound can be, we can heal through art and the wound does not overshadow. The wound is a thick scar, more robust than the original flesh.
Incentivize stewardship
Create/consume in concert with nature
Don’t make new.  Redistribute what we already have.

We have abandoned the distinction between self and other. We are living mutual responsibility with one another. Everything around us is us. We are pure selfless beings. Everything is rooted in selfless ness. We are selfless beings. We all have value to contribute to the world we are in. We treat each other and the world itself with mutuality. Everyone has something to contribute. There aren’t “roles” per se. There are energy beings that all have something that everyone else needs so we are one being. We all feel valuable and necessary.
Access to education, resources, living on purpose and with purpose exists for all. We live in highly agricultural, highly communal societies.
What we call jobs, are our talents put into practice, we love what we do.
Everything we do in the planet is taken into consideration for the impact in the future.

Being present and connected to all living things is prioritized, encouraged, practiced, and taught. We are creating and caring for our home Somewhere over the Rainbow continuously together. We are in touch with our bodies, minds and spirits and from this place we understand justice, safety and peace. We are learning how to generate, share, and infuse brilliant energy with everything we encounter. We see ourselves and each other as vital, magical and essential to this place and act and interact from that place.

Difference among individuals and communities is valued and honored. History is looked at with an honest lens, learning from our past, but not letting it cast a shadow on our future. Knowledge, both formal and informal, is respected and revered more than material items. The value of an individual or a community is based on how they treat each other versus how much money is in their bank account.
Although people have different opinions and viewpoints or some none at all, they are able to have conversations around the table about topics that may not be the easiest.
Our agriculture, community, etc is not taken for granted. We unite as one to make this earth a healthy, livable, and attainable environment.

People are popping out of gardens to say hi to one another. Groups of people do their chores together, singing. There are groups of people harvesting, and other people preparing food. Importantly, Apex predators are back.
We are just helping all the time. Instead of having labor as traditional labor, we work to provide. We only work a couple of hours out of the month, those who are able.
We’re back to fishing the way we used to, music is everywhere.
Work is an act of love, aligned with personal purpose and planetary care.
We met and continue to meet - at an extraordinary inflection point or fulcrum point in America and the world. And at our first gathering the first feeling is that of community!

It is a choice - to imagine creative thriving. And it takes courage. And we named our doubts and our fears. Is it worth it? Are we worth it? Even contemplating if it would be better for the Earth and other beings to let this world burn.
With the knowledge of what has been tried and failed, we decide to try something new.
We know closed systems die and old paradigms will not bring forth new ideas without a catalyst.

Where the laws of 2025 focus on control and order and benefit a few, we made a choice to reimagine. We wondered aloud about the tensions between the rules of land and the rules of the heavens. We wondered how to move through tensions.
We embrace collective consciousness. We make room for all voices. We share values and resources. We practice collaboration.
Part of life now, part of human essence, is what people produce together and use together. This includes food, clothing, wine, and furniture.
Everyone has a role to play and everyone contributes to their ability and capacity the group cares for those without the ability to care for themselves

We share resources and barter. 

We are a true, free, loving collective. 

Everyone feels seen, heard and is appreciated for the gifts they bring.
Melt the guns to build the bridges
Every adult has a responsibility to give back, even while we each take, no one is depleted and we have an accountability to each other and the roles we hold.
Labor is for the whole of the community, not for the individual needs as the needs of the community are taken care of by the community.

Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing there is a field. I’ll meet you there. When the soul lies down in that grass the world is too full to talk about. Ideas, language, even the phrase each other doesn’t make any sense.
No jobs.
No jobs, just shared roles of holding our societal and logistical needs.

There is Love for each other, our land. There is belief in what’s possible, in something higher than ourselves. Remembering from our own and other’s past. Repair, decentering of whiteness, cooperative economics, music, dance, healthy food, water, healing.
Labor supports life. People are part of nature not above it.
We don't marginalize those that are struggling. Rivers are undammed. Women, children, queer folks are protected. We shifted away from extraction as the way of relating to the Earth.
The roles in which people aspire most to are rooted in how best one can positively contribute to the well-being of others without ignoring one's own need.

Ownership/stewardship is individual and collective too.  No one wants to share a pair of shoes collectively.  Some want to weave and sell.   Some farm, some build, some repair, some teach, some learn, some do many things.

There is a flowing of resources, skills, jobs, places, and opportunities that allows each one to work, make their way, use their agency and creativity to live in and create value, provisions, and wellbeing.
Work is valued in all its forms.  It’s not about a specific job…but the weaving of them all.
People with disabilities know their contributions are honored and necessary.
People work in order to contribute to common values.  We know that every role matters.
Systems are aligned and in relationship.  For example, if school is off, work is off.  There is aligned timing – work, school, family, and government.
In work there will be less disconnect between knowledge, skill, and values.  The community will have great ways of on-ramping and off ramping people from work.
Automation has made the work week 20 hours.
The work you do is what you love and enjoy.

Despite being difficult and inconvenient by standards of the past – all labor is enjoyable and fulfilling because it is intelligently aligned with domicile, life, and living conditions (in contrast to the mismatches of the past which struggled to match “jobs” with “cost of living”). Yet since people don’t have to travel for work, time (like so many other things) is abundant. This abundance of time is applied to honing crafts, healing, fishing, walking (as a practice) and composing songs.

People choose jobs they want to do and that correlate with their passions.  We cycle between different jobs throughout the year, depending on what is needed in a given season. Imagine waking up and going to your job as a bus driver, and then, after a few months, switching to your other job as a chef at a restaurant. All throughout this time, you still have enough free time to do your hobbies and explore your passions after work, like painting and birdwatching.  No one is without work if they want it because everyone mostly have part-time jobs.

We contribute to the functioning of society while meeting our individual needs and desires.  We don’t have to sacrifice one in order to do the other.

What jobs do you imagine in the future?  What might your descendants be doing?
I want that in 150 years, people’s salaries will be enough so they don’t have to overwork just to buy a house, a car, or the home of their dreams.
Mutual stewardship. Land as center of gravity. We all have roles in our community and are deeply sacred and essential to the make up of our ecosystem.
No money.  More time for creativity, music, art.

People are oriented to bringing forward their gifts on behalf of their community not interested in seeking personal wealth or fame because those pursuits are known as mental illness and tread with care.
Parents can live lift not shackled to a job just to make ends meet to be able to invest in something bigger.
The future no longer runs on clock systems.  People do the work that follows their passion.  The school system now prepares to foster curiosity, nature based learning, relationship with nature.
As adults people follow passion or follow different careers aligned with their passions.
There is still hard work, but with dignity and abundance of time.
Creativity is prioritized as a human need and we know how to build and fix things. We pass on our knowledge and skills.
We still need some factories to produce some goods but they're all owned by the employees. We are mindful of providing salaries that seem even, fair, consistent.

We don’t make sharp delineations between work and hobbies. People pursue activities in their life that bring joy and meaning first and foremost and can choose multiple things and skills to have at the same time. We know that art is not just a leisure thing but something we see as necessary for human flourishing
We now understand science as one pathway to wisdom. Patents are not owned by individuals or corporations but given to the common good.

There would be lots of places like Maker’s Space that engages the value of creating things or doing things with your hands.  The whole community would filter through these places.  Learn things…build community.  Teachers and mentors would be plentiful.
Some old structures will be perfect…some will be a mess…because lots of people will help build and maintain everything.  They will do their best.
LIfe is slow things take time to make and do and thats ok
Some people work very hard because they love what they do. Some people don’t. Some people contribute to community. Life outcomes are the same.
Barangay model of self reliance: for and by community of neighbors, friends, and family

Work has been repurposed to mean the collective remembering of how to restore balance with all our relations. It follows a seasonal calendar, involves travel, play, and sacred duty and there is a role for everyone! I can’t wait to go to work!
We no longer work for wages, our work is the daily care of each other and the collective
We each have a craft/trade to contribute in 3d real life; we learn this at free school.
Jobs that are tedious are not tedious because they’re done in community.

People know about their neighbors’ resources and skills. Mobility aid and assistive equipment do not require documentation for access. They are creative, beautiful and have aesthetic considerations. Housing,education etc. is created from materials, labor and resources that communities are in active relationship with. Natural building – ways of constructing temp regulating structures based on the land, soil, climate of a place.
People’s senses have become heightened by doing the practical things needed in community.  We communicate through senses.
Everyone’s natural strengths are positively utilized.  There is a collective sharing of resources.  We barter and trade.

Grass fields like highways. A big park. My future is me. Healing myself, preparing myself to project and give to others. I love for people to know what is there. Healing oneself to project onto others. You give everything. Knowing about everything in order to give.
Original of Translation: Pastos como carreteras. Un parque grande. Mi futuro es yo. Curarme, prepararme para proyectar y darle a los demás. Me encanta que la gente sepa lo que hay. Sanada uno para proyectar a los demás. Das todo. Saber de todo para dar.

Content: We should preserve our mountains. In the future there will be more schools and fewer prisons. More knowledge. When we are united, we fight inequality. United we achieve many goals.
Original of Translation: Deberiamos de preservar nuestras montañas. En el futuro habrá más escuelas y menos prisiones. Más conocimiento. Cuando estamos Unidos combatimos la desigualdad. Unidos ganamos muchas metas.

Content: I envision waking up in the morning with my day not decided for me but me deciding what my day will look like. A day where people’s lives aren’t punitive. A time where spending time loving your family and building a legacy and future for them isn’t determined by affordability or nepotism. I imagine a spirit of Love that doesn’t sleep until it knows that you and yours are well. A culture where we meet each other’s needs and and not only pray about them. I imagine mankind being more valuable than the parasite of greed and selfishness.

When access to health and wellness isn’t based on affordability, accessibility, a government program, or worthiness but necessity. Where everyone can value each other and each other’s needs as their own responsibility. A time where you take all that you need and not all that you want. A time where no one’s wants come at the expense of another’s needs or wants. A time of peace and safety for women and children, where no one has to think about their loved ones being hurt or taken advantage of.

A time where we can trust one another to make the decision in the best interest of one another. We are a village raising our future together. A place where 3rd World countries don’t exist. People wouldn’t come to America for freedom because there will be freedom everywhere. I feel reassured. Thriving now.

Trust, hope, fulfillment of human potential are the universal goals. Respect for others is taught in all spaces. Cultural exchange is encouraged in all structures and systems, food, commercial, education and with equal values.

Joy is hilarious! I carry resentment for resistance as joyful. It can be an excuse to not do the hard work- prioritize one's own sense of well being over collective. If I had a word for our descendents- joy stemming from health, wholenes, beauty, diversity, deep meaningful connection with the sources of life.

We focused on how we reach our shared potential. We also focused on freedom. Freedom of motion (no passports). Freedom to love. Freedom to change jobs, locations, and hobbies. The freedom that comes with having enough resources to thrive. We reject restrictions and embrace being able to go where you want AND be who you want. We also enjoy the freedom to party!

Work happens. And when it does, it is rooted in the desire to serve the community or live out your purpose. Work is not based on threats or risks of starvation or homelessness. Work days are shorter and work is balanced.  There is still much work to do – but we know what work needs to be done. We’ve been able to stop guessing at what we need. We know. We’ve stopped worrying about making mistakes. We find our grounding in who we are and the world we are proud to be a part of. We know that a good future rests on a good present.

Child is running around playing in a park while family and community has a potluck. No one is worried that it’s a Sunday because we all enjoy what we do and where we work and get to choose what we do.

Sketch of the world’s values benign rooted in transparency and pursuing difficult work. Have to go through the difficult work to get meaning and purpose. Learning by the water. World rooted in accountability so that when we blossom, maturity looks like care and being by water and under the moon eating with their families.
Being loud/shouting for our needs, resources, and our collective healing. Loud in our needs with better funded education, community spaces and funding...branching out
Repair, accountability and rebuilding is everyone's responsibility. We see and care for each other as a global community.

Accessibility was what initially came to mind when we first began. It seemed to be a recurring word that popped into my head when thinking about education (especially youth), even transportation. Folks feeling and having what they need to thrive. Accessibility to mental health for youth. Someone they can talk to, when they have need.
We can do all the things if we do it TOGETHER! Lahat ay magagawa kapag tayong lahat ay sama-sama!

Date/Circle Name: 8/18/26 A New Way of Life Los Angeles
Content: Plenty of abundance. Pure investment in humanity. Invest in people, making sure people have their needs met.
People are excited to work with each other.

People spend a lot of time enjoying nature because they don’t have jobs to make money. Folks have work they need to do that supports community thriving, but no one has to work to survive. And of course, a statue of Ben!
Ancestral wisdom guides our day-to-day decisions.
Original of Translation: La sabiduría ancestral guía nuestras decisiones de dia a dia.

Content: We humans speak to each other with positive words.
Original of Translation: Los humanos nos hablamos con palabras positivas.

Content: We are a species of animals that thrives because we help one another.
Original of Translation: Nosotros como especie de animales que prospera porque se ayudan entre ellos mismos.

Content: The greatest wealth is kindness. Success is not measured by what someone  owns but by how much good they do.
Dignified work
We will learn to grow our own food, can, sew, repair our own things, build things by hand, raise chickens, preserve our own meat.
We will learn to start anew with the opportunity to create/build with others for the greater good of the community.
